Judgment:
1. The present is a complaint filed under section 16 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954
(herein after referred to as Pfa Act), alleging that the accused have violated the provisions of t
he PFA Act and Rules.

2. As per the complaint, on 27.12.2001 the Food Inspector Virendra Singh purchased a sample of 'Dal Arhar" a food article for analysis from accused Manohar Lal Wadhwa at M/s Wadhwa Store,
Shop No. 128, Guru Nanak Market, Karol Bagh, New Delhi - 5, where the said food article was found stored for sale and where accused No.1 Manohar Lal Wadhwa was found conducting the business of the said food article at the time of sampling.
The sample consisted 750 gms of dal arhar taken from an open gunny bag having no label declaration.
The sample was taken under the supervision / direction of Sh.Surender Kumar, SDM/LHA.
The sample was taken after properly mixing the dal arhar with the help of clean and dry jhaba.
The Food Inspector divided the sample then and there into three equal parts by putting them in three separate clean and dry bottles.
Each bottle was separately packed, fastened and sealed according to PFA Act and Rules.
The vendor's signatures were obtained on the LHA slip and the wrapper of the sample bottles.
Notice was given to accused No. 1 Manohar Lal Wadhwa and the price of sample was also given to DA vs Manohar Lal Wadhwa etc. him vide vendor receipt dated 27.12.2001.
Panchnama too was prepared at the spot.
All the documents prepared by F.I. were signed by accused NO. 1 Manohar Lal Wadhwa and the other witness Sh N.N. Sharma, FI,

Before starting sample proceeding efforts were made to join public witnesses but none came (award, as such Sh N.N. Sharma, FI was joined as witness.
3. One counter-part of the sample bearing LHA code No. SK/LHA/001142 was also sent to Public Analyst, Delhi in intact condition and two counter-parts were deposited with the LHA in intact condition.
Public Analyst analysed the sample and found the same to be adulterated.

The report of the Public Analyst is as follows:
"The sample is adulterated because it is coloured with synthetic colouring matter viz tartarzine."
4.

It is the case of the complainant that accused No. 1 Manohar Lal Wadhwa was the vendor-cum-proprietor of M/s Wadhwa Store, Shop No. 128, Guru Nanak Market, Karol Bagh, New Delhi - 5 , at the time of sampling and as such he was incharge of and responsible for day to day conduct of the business of the said shop.
5. Thereafter on completion of investigation, sanction under section 20 of the PFA Act was obtained from the Director PFA.

The complaint was then filed in the court on 07.11.2002 alleging violation of section 2i(a)(j)&(m) and Rule 23 read with Rule 28 & 29 of PFA Rules, 1955 as punishable section 7/16(1)(a) of PFA Act against the accused.

During the trial, vide order dated DA vs Manohar Lal Wadhwa etc. 30.04.2010 accused No. 2 M/s Ram Bhagat Prem Chand, accused No. 3 Mangat Rai,

2 accused No. 4 Pankaj Gupta and accused No. 5 Sachin Gupta were also impleaded and summoned as suppliers to accused no.1.
6.
As the complaint was filed in writing by a public servant, recording of pre-summoning evidence was dispensed with and the accused was summoned initially and later on other accused were also summoned.
The accused no.1 thereafter exercised his option of analysing the counter part through CFL under section 13 (2) of the PFA Act.

Based on the report of the CFL as well as evidence led in pre charge evidence, charge was framed against the accused for commission of the offence punishable under section 7/16(1) (a) PFA Act being violation of Section 2(ia)(a)(b)(j)&(m) of PFA Act and Rule 23 and 29 of PFA Rules, 1955, to which accused pleaded not guilty and claimed trial.
7. At the trial, the prosecution examined four witness in support of its case i.e. PW-1 FI Sh. Virender Singh, PW-2 SDM/LHA Sh. Surender Kumar, PW-3 FI Sh. Gian Chand and PW-4 FI Sh. N.N Sharma.
PW-1 FI Virender Singh and PW-4 FI N.N. Sharma were part of the team that had visited the spot for sample proceedings under the supervision of SDM/LHA Sh. Surender Kumar.

These witness narrated the steps undertaken by them during the sample proceedings, including disclosing their identity, expressing intention to purchase sample for analysis, lifting the sample commodity of "Dal Arhar" 750 gms from the vendor for analysis, bearing no label or declaration, taking the sample of Dal Arhar and mixing help of a clean & dry jhaba, dividing the sample DA vs Manohar Lal Wadhwa etc. into three equal parts by putting them into three separate clean and dry sample bottles, separately sealing, packing and marking the same and obtaining signatures of vendor and witnesses.

They also proved the necessary documents including the vendor's receipt Ex.PW-1/A,
Notice Ex. PW-1/B, Panchnama Ex. PW-1/C.
The accused also made statement Ex.PW1/D alongwith photocopy of MCD Registration Ex.PW1/G.
Thereafter, one counterpart of the sample along with one copy of memo in form VII and another copy of memo in form VII in sealed deposited with PA vide receipt Ex.PW1/D on 28.12.2001.

The remaining two counter parts of the sample in intact condition along with two copies of memo of Form VII in a sealed packet were deposited with LHA vide LHA Receipt Ex. PW1/E, under intimation that one counterpart of the same has already been deposited with PA.
Thereafter, PA Report Ex.PW1/F was received, according to which the sample was adulterated because the same was coloured with synthetic colouring matter tartrazine.
Thereafter PW-1 collected reply from STO vide Ex.PW1/H.
After completion of investigation, the entire case file was put before then Director PFA for obtaining his Consent.
The then Director PFA granted his Consent for prosecution vide sanction order Ex.PW1/J.
Thereafter, the present complaint Ex.PW1/K was filed before the Court by PW-3 FI Sh. Gyan Chand.
Then intimation letter Ex.PW1/L alongwith copy of PA Reports was sent to the accused vide postal receipt.
These witnesses were duly cross-examined by Ld. Defence Counsel.
8. Statement of the accused under section 313 CrPC were recorded wherein the accused persons denied the allegations and pleaded DA vs Manohar Lal Wadhwa etc. innocence.

sentences.text: Thereafter matter was listed for defence evidence.
9. In their defence, the accused no.1 examined Sh Yograj as DW-1.
The accused No. 1 Manohar Lal Wadhwa also examined himself as DW-2.
Thereafter defence evidence was closed vide order dated 10.09.2013 and the matter was fixed for final arguments.

10. In a criminal case, the burden is on the prosecution to prove its case against the accused beyond reasonable doubt by leading positive evidence.
This burden cannot be shifted to the accused and it has to be necessary discharged by the prosecution itself.

11.It is to be understood that the charge framed against the accused is for violation of section 2(i)(a),(b) (j) and (m) of the PFA Act read with Rules 23 and 29 of PFA Rules with respect to 'adulteration'.

Under section 2(ia)(a) of PFA Act, the prosecution has to establish that the purchaser had demanded a food article of a specific nature, substance or quality and the article sold was, to his prejudice, either not of the nature, substance or quality demanded, or was not of the nature,
substance or quality which it purported or represented to be. Section 2(ia)(j) specifically deals with colouring matter which is present other than prescribed or is present beyond the prescribed limits of variability.

Section 2(ia)
(m) of PFA Act deals with situation where the quality or purity of an article falls below the prescribed standard or its constituents are present in quantities not within the prescribed limits of variability.
12.The commodity in the present case is Dal Arhar which is food DA vs Manohar Lal Wadhwa etc.
grain and has to be tested as per the standards prescribed for food grains.
It is clear that this article falls in Item A.18.06.09 of Appendix B to the PFA Rules.
Both the analysts have applied the same standards to this product.
It is nowhere the stand of the accused that the food article does not fall under this head or that it falls under some other head.
13. It is pertinent to note that both the chemical experts, PA and CFL, have found the presence of the synthetic colouring matter Tartrazine which is a totally prohibited item in the sample analysed.
On this point, both the reports are in conformity to each other and not at variance.
14. The defence taken by the accused No. 1, the vendor is that he had purchased this dal from M/s Ram Bhagat Prem Chand of Sadar Bazar through broker Sh. Yog Raj.
According to accused No. 1 he had purchased the dal vide bill Ex.DA.
However the defence of rest of the is that the dal in question does not belong to him, it might have been purchased by accused No. 1 from somewhere else.
The accused No. 1 has placed on record the bill Ex.DA in his evidence.
The accused No. 1 has also put this question to PW-1 the Food Inspector, but he deposed that accused No. 1 had not informed that he had purchased the dal ahrar from M/s Ram Bhagat Prem Chand .
15.It is pertinent to note that no such bill/invoice/cash memo of purchase of this Dal had been shown to the FI or the name of the supplier disclosed to him at the time of sampling.

Even if his stand is accepted that the FI had refused to accept the bill at the DA vs Manohar Lal Wadhwa etc.
spot though there is no evidence to this effect, still nothing had prevented him from sending the documents to the PFA department at any time thereafter at the first available opportunity or even during the course of investigation.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: No such stand was taken or name of the supplier disclosed even in letter Ex.PW-1/D given by the accused No.1 to the FI, so as to enable the FI to investigate the role of the supplier and to implicate or exonerate it.
When the complainant was not even informed about the particulars of the supplier, the accused cannot say that the FI did not verify the facts.

Da vs Manohar Lal Wadhwa Etc. on 18 July, 2018 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/117099120/
4 16.
Be that as it may, it would be no defence available to the accused to claim that he was not the manufacturer of the commodity in question or that he was only a retailer using the same.
A seller or packer or distributor or manufacturer would operate in different fields and all of them can be held liable in their separate areas.
Sale of adulterated food article is prohibited.

The definition of 'sale'
under section 2 (xiii) is very wide which includes storing or exposing for sale as a retailer and even attempt to sell and also sale for analysis.

The only benefit which the accused can claim on this ground is under section 19(2) of PFA Act which would apply only if he is able to show that he had purchased the product against a warranty and had been selling the product in the same manner as purchased by him.
17.Even
if the documents relied upon by him are accepted, that would not come to his rescue.
There is nothing to connect the lifted sample of dal arhar to the dal allegedly purchased through these documents bill Ex.DA.
The dal was lifted from an open DA vs Manohar Lal Wadhwa etc. gunny bag bearing no label declaration.

entities.text: DA vs Manohar Lal Wadhwa etc. gunny bag
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Thus, there is nothing to show that the dal lifted from the shop, was the same dal, which the accused had allegedly purchased vide bill Ex.DA placed on record by him or any particular bill amongst these bills.
18. Even otherwise, the bill produced by the accused do not qualify to give warranty to the accused under section 19(2) of the PFA Act.
For that, specific language is to be used as per Rule 12-A and as per Form-VIA, PFA Rules.

Reliance in this regard can be placed on M/s. Muralidhar Shyamlal v.
State of Assam [1996(I) PFA Cases 86].

entities.text:
M/s. Muralidhar Shyamlal v.
State of Assam [1996(I) PFA Cases 86]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: There is no batch number / code number or any other means to identify the dal sold to be the one lifted.
Again, the bill/invoice should carry a warranty in the prescribed language.

Without commenting on the correctness of the language and or legality of such claim of evasion of liability under the PFA Act, it is certain that the warranty as prescribed by Rule 12-A and Form VI- A of PFA Rules is not there on the bill.

19.Further, it is to be understood that the benefit of warranty under section 19(2) of PFA Act would be available only when there is a written warranty from the supplier/seller in addition to the fact that it has been sold in the same condition as was purchased.
Both the conditions have to be fulfilled simultaneously.
There is further no evidence to the effect that the dal was in same state or condition when sold/used.
There is no witness who could depose that the dal lifted from possession of the accused was in the same condition as was purchased though the bill in question.
On the contrary its written on the bill there the seller is not responsible for the goods after sale.
Thus, even the benefit of warranty cannot be DA vs Manohar Lal Wadhwa etc. extended to the accused no. 1 in this case.

sentences.text:
20. The case in hand would be therefore covered under section 2(ia)
(a) of PFA Act as there is evidence to show that it was not of the nature, substance or quality which it is purported to be as per PFA Rules.
The case would fall under section 2(ia)(j) as there is presence of colour which is not permitted in this article.
Violation of section 2(ia)(j) is punishable under section 16(1A) and violation of section 2(ia)(a) is punishable under section 16(i)(a) of PFA Act.
But being graver offence, conviction can be under section 16(1A) of PFA Act.

Da vs Manohar Lal Wadhwa Etc. on 18 July, 2018 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/117099120/
5 21.
Having said so, it can be said that the complainant / prosecution has been able to establish its case and prove the guilt of the accused No. 1 beyond the shadow of reasonable doubt.

It has been proved that the accused no. 1 had sold adulterated food in violation of section 2(ia)(a) and (j) of PFA Act read with Rules 23, 28 and 29 of PFA Rules, and has committed the offence punishable under section 7/16(1A) of PFA Act.
22.
Thus, the accused No. 1 is held guilty and convicted for the offence punishable under section 16(1A) of the PFA Act.
The rest of the accused are acquitted.
Let the matter be listed for arguments on sentence on behalf of accused No.1.
